parts.text: Which claim is always true for every integer $a$?

options.text: $1\times a=a$ and $-1\times a=-a$, where $-a$ is the additive inverse of $a$.
The answer is the factor $-1$, with no product stated.
$-1\times a=a$, because the printed numeral $1$ is kept and the minus is dropped.
$-1\times a=-a$ only when $a$ is already positive.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem: Rachna multiplies any integer $a$ by $1$ or by $-1$ on her number line practice sheet.

part_answers.answer: For every integer $a$, multiplying by $1$ leaves $a$ unchanged, and multiplying by $-1$ gives the additive inverse $-a$.

teacher.key_rationale: Always 1×a=a and (−1)×a=−a. Naming −1 alone substitutes a label. Dropping the minus is surface capture. Restricting −a to positive a omits that −a may be positive when a is negative.
